Closed reduction is an effective and generally easy-to-perform treatment for nasal fractures, especially in mild cases. It involves manually manipulating the bones in the nose to restore their original position. Early intervention can lead to improved patient satisfaction rates.

However, it's essential to note that closed reduction may not be suitable or safe for more severe or complex nasal fractures, such as those with significant rotational deformity or extension of the distal fragment. In such cases, surgical intervention may be necessary to achieve optimal outcomes.

Additionally, some patients may experience numbness or other complications following nasal microfat grafting, a treatment used to restore sensation in the nasal tip after septoplasty. The duration of numbness can vary, with most patients experiencing partial recovery over a 3-month period.
